title: Ancient India in Brief
summary: A fast journey through the Indus cities, the great kingdoms and the gifts of ancient Indian scholars.

steps.title: The first cities
sentences: About four and a half thousand years ago, cities such as Harappa and Mohenjo-daro grew in the Indus Valley.
They had planned streets, drains and busy trade.
Later, other kingdoms grew along the Ganga plains and in the south.

steps.title: Great rulers
sentences: Ashoka of the Maurya dynasty ruled much of India more than two thousand years ago.
The Cholas of Tamil Nadu ruled for centuries and built the great temple at Thanjavur, completed around the year 1010.
Their ships sailed across the sea, and they traded with faraway lands.

steps.title: Learning and ideas
sentences: Indian scholars helped develop the number system we use today, including the idea of zero as a number.
Aryabhata wrote about astronomy and maths in the year 499.
Sushruta wrote about surgery, and Charaka about medicine, in ancient times.

steps.title: Why it matters
sentences: The ideas we use every day, like our digits, came to the rest of the world through many peoples.
Learning how they spread shows that knowledge belongs to everyone.
History is the story of people borrowing, adding and sharing ideas.

facts: The shape of the digits 0 to 9 we use today developed from Indian numerals and travelled to the West through Arab scholars.
Brihadisvara Temple in Thanjavur has a tower about 66 metres tall.
The Ashoka Chakra on India's flag comes from the lion capital at Sarnath.

quiz.q: Which ancient civilisation had cities like Harappa?
quiz.why: Harappa was an Indus Valley city.

quiz.q: Which dynasty built the Brihadisvara Temple at Thanjavur?
quiz.why: The Cholas built it around the year 1010.

quiz.q: Which idea did Indian mathematicians help develop?
quiz.why: Indian mathematicians treated zero as a number and used it in calculation.

notes: Years are as commonly taught; the temple was consecrated around 1010 CE.
